commit_message: GATE-05: service negotiation and route commitment — distinct route types + acceptance signatures
scope_completed: ServiceRequirement (what the initiator needs: capability, destination, maxHops, bandwidth, expiry)
CapabilityOffer (node declares it CAN do — ≠ available ≠ authorized per spec/00 §21)
checkPolicy() with all spec/09 §3 guards: LINK_UP required, ADV_VERIFIED rejected, SSRF/loopback/private/allowlist checks, peer revocation, capability match, expiry
checkCapacity() with connections, global/per-peer quota, bandwidth checks
ServiceAgreement (result of successful policy + capacity checks; binds node to providing service)
RouteHop (requires nodeId, capability, endpoint, linkUp=true, serviceAgreement)
RouteProposal (initiator proposes path; source signature ≠ participant acceptance per spec/00 §23)
RouteAcceptance (each hop independently signs; binds routeId, hopIndex, acceptorNodeId, expiry)
RouteCommitment (ALL hops accepted → commit; validates every hop has acceptance, correct acceptor, LINK_UP, not expired)
CommittedRoute (ONLY from RouteCommitment; the ONLY object that can create a circuit)
TOPOLOGY_TO_ROUTE_FORBIDDEN architecture guard (topology/Dijkstra → route is forbidden per spec/00 §31)
PROPOSAL_TO_CIRCUIT_FORBIDDEN architecture guard (RouteProposal → circuit without commitment is forbidden)
20 unit tests covering all policy/capacity/route scenarios
protocol_adr_references: spec/07-routing.md (routing pipeline: discovery → proposal → acceptance → commitment → circuit)
spec/09-internet-gateway.md §2 (gateway model: capability ≠ policy ≠ authorization ≠ capacity)
spec/00 §22 (routing: discovery ≠ path validation ≠ route ≠ circuit)
spec/00 §23 (route objects: proposal, acceptance, commitment, committed route)
known_limitations: Real-process A → Relay → Gateway integration test is deferred — the unit tests prove the protocol-core correctness with in-memory keypairs. The integration test will exercise the mini-services once they support the 3-message handshake and route negotiation.

ServiceAgreement.requirementDigest and RouteProposal.agreementDigest are currently placeholder random values. A follow-up should compute them as BLAKE3-256 hashes of the actual ServiceRequirement and hop service agreements.
Route commitment does not yet verify acceptance signatures cryptographically (only checks structural validity). A follow-up should add verifyRouteAcceptance calls in createRouteCommitment.
